sources.title: Recommender Systems with Generative Retrieval
sources.verified_from: arXiv API record (title/abstract/PDF links); full-text HTML endpoint
sources.exact_overlap: Generative retrieval for recommendation: user interaction histories are used to generate item identifiers (semantic IDs) as recommendations. Direct overlap with user next-item behavior and generative IDs.
sources.not_established: No hyperbolic geometry is identified as a method in this work; therefore it does not establish the three-way intersection.

sources.title: Hyperbolic Graph Convolutional Neural Networks
sources.verified_from: arXiv abstract record; full text not independently inspected for this task
sources.exact_overlap: Uses hyperbolic geometry for graph representation learning, relevant as a geometric-method precedent for hierarchical graph data.
sources.not_established: Not evidence of generative semantic IDs or user next-item recommendation; the overlap is only the geometry component.

sources.title: Bridging Search and Recommendation in Generative Retrieval: Does One Task Help the Other?
sources.verified_from: arXiv API record (title/abstract/PDF links); full-text HTML endpoint
sources.exact_overlap: Generative recommendation directly associates model inputs with item IDs and studies joint generative search/recommendation; relevant to generative-ID recommendation and behavioral recommendation settings.
sources.not_established: Abstract does not establish hyperbolic geometry or specifically next-item prediction.

behavior_problem_candidates.candidate: Given a user's chronologically ordered interaction history, predict the next item by autoregressively generating its semantic ID.
behavior_problem_candidates.hyperbolic_connection: Potential research question, not an established result: place items or semantic-ID prefixes in a hyperbolic space to represent hierarchical item/category structure, then test whether this improves next-item generation.

behavior_problem_candidates.candidate: Model user-specific transitions and multi-level item hierarchy jointly, rather than only modeling item content or global popularity.
behavior_problem_candidates.hyperbolic_connection: A synthesis/hypothesis across distinct literatures; neither cited source verifies the combined method.

limitations: No independently verified source located here demonstrates all three elements together: user next-item behavior, hyperbolic geometry, and generative semantic IDs. Treat the intersection as an apparent research gap, not a novelty claim.

FULL_TEXT labels indicate an arXiv full-text HTML/PDF is openly linked and the record supports the stated overlap; the hyperbolic source is labeled ABSTRACT because its full text was not independently inspected in this run.
Semantic IDs are sometimes called item IDs or code/token sequences; do not assume every generative-retrieval paper uses semantic IDs in the same technical sense.
This is a bounded literature scan, not an exhaustive systematic review; absence of a direct intersection paper is not proof none exists.
